Analysis.object: Emotion dysregulation is an expected possible risk factor for both exercise addiction and eating disorders. The difficulties in emotion regulation strongly meduated the relationship between psychological symptoms and eating disorders in Female and explained 52.7% of the total indirect effect compared to the much lower 17.3% in male.

We adopted a cross sectional design and we conducted statistical mediation analyses. Although mediation might assume any casual relationships, our design and data are not suitable for confirming any cause and effect relationships. Furthermore, our model is based solely on theoretical assumptions and the current design cannot help to refute neither the alternative not the possible equivalent models. The nature of self rating instruments implies several possible biases (social desirability, insufficient self knowledge, distorsion of the memory processes) we should consider in interprating the results. Using self report questionnaire by collecting data at the same time from the same individuals raises the bias of common method variance. We used screening methods for assessing both eating disorders and exercise addiction, and these instruments are not applicable for making diagnoses. The SCOFF questionnaire showed a questionable internal consistency in the present sample. We examined a wide range of regular exercisers which may down tune the exposed results, since in a group of high-volume exercisers the current findings may possibly be amplified.
This study should be replicated with avid exercisers training for at least 10hr or more per week.

Population.object: Members of various urban fitness centers aged between 18 and 60 years
